Source.Chapter: II - Rules of the road (Articles 5 to 34)
Source.Text: United Nations Treaty Series, Chapter XI.B.19 (https://treaties.un.org/doc/Treaties/1977/05/19770524%2000-13%20AM/Ch_XI_B_19.pdf), English text as signed in 1968

Amendments.Name: Amendments in force 1993-09-03 and 2006-03-28 (consolidated text ECE/TRANS/195)
Amendments.Note: not included: the UNECE consolidated text could not be downloaded; the articles below are the 1968 text

Amendments.Name: Article 8 paragraph 5bis and Article 39 (driver assistance systems)
Amendments.Note: not included: text not at hand

Rules.Title: Status of signs and signals
Rules.Text: Road-users shall comply with the instructions conveyed by road signs, traffic light signals and road markings even if the said instructions appear to contradict other traffic regulations.

Rules.Title: Lights over priority signs
Rules.Text: Instructions conveyed by traffic light signals shall take precedence over those conveyed by road signs regulating priority.

Rules.Title: Obey authorized officials
Rules.Text: Road-users shall promptly obey all instructions given by authorized officials directing traffic.

Rules.Title: Officials over signs, lights and rules
Rules.Text: The instructions given by authorized officials directing traffic shall take precedence over those conveyed by road signs, traffic light signals and road markings, and over traffic regulations.

Rules.Title: General rule: no danger, no obstruction
Rules.Text: Road-users shall avoid any behaviour likely to endanger or obstruct traffic, to endanger persons, or to cause damage to public or private property.

Rules.Title: Objects on the road
Rules.Text: Road-users shall not obstruct traffic or risk making it dangerous by throwing, depositing or leaving any object or substance on the road; if unable to avoid it, they shall remove it as soon as possible or warn other road-users.

Rules.Title: Every moving vehicle has a driver
Rules.Text: Every moving vehicle or combination of vehicles shall have a driver.

Rules.Title: Fitness to drive
Rules.Text: Every driver shall possess the necessary physical and mental ability and be in a fit physical and mental condition to drive.

Rules.Title: Knowledge and skill
Rules.Text: Every driver of a power-driven vehicle shall possess the knowledge and skill necessary for driving the vehicle.

Rules.Title: Always in control
Rules.Text: Every driver shall at all times be able to control his vehicle or to guide his animals.

Rules.Title: Flocks and herds in sections
Rules.Text: Flocks and herds should be divided into sections of moderate length spaced sufficiently far apart for the convenience of traffic.

Rules.Title: One direction of traffic in a State
Rules.Text: The direction of traffic shall be the same on all roads in a State except, where appropriate, on roads used solely or principally by through traffic between two other States.

Rules.Title: Keep near the edge of the traffic side
Rules.Text: Every driver of a vehicle shall, to the extent permitted by circumstances, keep his vehicle near the edge of the carriageway appropriate to the direction of traffic.

Rules.Title: Not the opposite carriageway
Rules.Text: Where a road comprises two or three carriageways, no driver shall take the carriageway situated on the side opposite to that appropriate to the direction of traffic.

Rules.Title: Not the opposite half of a wide two-way carriageway
Rules.Text: On two-way carriageways having four or more lanes, no driver shall take the lanes entirely on the opposite half; on three lanes, not the lane at the opposite edge.

Rules.Title: Overtake on the side opposite to the traffic side
Rules.Text: Drivers overtaking shall do so on the side opposite to that appropriate to the direction of traffic; on the traffic side if the driver overtaken has signalled and moved over to turn to the other side.

Rules.Title: Before overtaking, make sure
Rules.Text: Before overtaking: no follower has begun to overtake; the driver ahead has not signalled to overtake; the lane is clear far enough ahead not to endanger or impede oncoming traffic; the driver can resume the position of Article 10, paragraph 3.

Rules.Title: No overtaking at a crest or blind bend
Rules.Text: Overtaking on two-way carriageways is prohibited when approaching the crest of a hill and, if visibility is inadequate, on bends, unless lanes marked as closed to oncoming traffic are used.

Rules.Title: Wide berth when overtaking
Rules.Text: When overtaking, a driver shall give the road-user or road-users overtaken a sufficiently wide berth.

Rules.Title: May stay in the overtaking lane
Rules.Text: With at least two lanes in his direction, a driver who would have to overtake again shortly after moving back may remain in the overtaking lane, without undue inconvenience to faster vehicles from behind.

Rules.Title: Lines of traffic
Rules.Text: In dense traffic moving in lines, a faster line is not overtaking; a driver not in the lane nearest the traffic-side edge may change lanes only to prepare to turn or to park.

Rules.Title: No straddling lane markings in lines
Rules.Text: When moving in lines, drivers are forbidden, if the lanes are indicated by longitudinal markings, to straddle these markings.

Rules.Title: No overtaking at intersections and level-crossings
Rules.Text: No driver shall overtake a vehicle other than a two-wheeler immediately before or on an intersection other than a roundabout (unless on the priority road, or traffic is directed by an official or lights), nor before or on a level-crossing without gates or half-gates.

Rules.Title: Overtaking near a pedestrian crossing
Rules.Text: A vehicle shall not overtake another approaching or stopped before a pedestrian crossing otherwise than at a speed low enough to stop immediately if a pedestrian is on the crossing.

Rules.Title: Let the follower overtake
Rules.Text: A driver who perceives that a following driver wishes to overtake shall keep close to the traffic-side edge and refrain from accelerating; a slow or bulky vehicle shall slow down and if necessary pull in.

Rules.Title: Passing on the traffic side in multi-lane roads
Rules.Text: Contracting Parties may, on one-way and on multi-lane carriageways with marked lanes, allow vehicles in one lane to overtake on the traffic side vehicles in another lane.

Rules.Title: Passing oncoming traffic
Rules.Text: When passing oncoming traffic, a driver shall leave sufficient lateral space and, if necessary, move close to the traffic-side edge; if impeded, he shall slow down and if necessary stop.

Rules.Title: Mountain roads: downhill gives way
Rules.Text: On mountain roads where passing is impossible or difficult, the driver travelling downhill pulls in to let the vehicle proceeding uphill pass, and reverses if one has to.

Rules.Title: Speed: stop within the forward vision
Rules.Text: Every driver shall have his vehicle under control and adjust its speed to the circumstances so as to be able to stop within his range of forward vision and short of any foreseeable obstruction; he shall slow down and if necessary stop when visibility is not good.

Rules.Title: Not abnormally slowly
Rules.Text: No driver shall impede the normal progress of other vehicles by travelling abnormally slowly without proper cause.

Rules.Title: Safe distance behind
Rules.Text: The driver of a vehicle moving behind another vehicle shall keep at a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid collision if the vehicle in front should suddenly slow down or stop.

Rules.Title: Heavy vehicles leave room to overtake
Rules.Text: Outside built-up areas, vehicles of more than 3,500 kg or more than 10 m keep such distance behind power-driven vehicles that overtaking vehicles can move into the space in front.

Rules.Title: Speed limits are domestic
Rules.Text: Nothing in this Convention prevents Contracting Parties from prescribing general or local speed limits, minimum and maximum speeds, or minimum intervals.

Rules.Title: Manoeuvres without risk
Rules.Text: A driver wishing to pull out, move over or turn shall first make sure that he can do so without risk of endangering other road-users behind, ahead or about to pass, having regard to their position, direction and speed.

Rules.Title: U-turn and reversing
Rules.Text: Any driver wishing to make a U-turn or to reverse shall first make sure that he can do so without endangering or impeding other road-users.

Rules.Title: Signal before and during
Rules.Text: Before turning or moving laterally, the driver shall give clear and sufficient warning by the direction-indicators, throughout the manoeuvre, ceasing when it is completed.

Rules.Title: Let buses move off from stops
Rules.Text: In built-up areas drivers should slow down and if necessary stop to allow public-transport vehicles to move off from marked stops.

Rules.Title: Position for turning
Rules.Text: Turning to the traffic side: keep close to that edge and turn tight; turning to the other side: move close to the centreline (or the opposite edge of a one-way carriageway) and enter the other road on its traffic side.

Rules.Title: Turning gives way to oncoming and to cycle tracks
Rules.Text: While changing direction, the driver shall allow oncoming vehicles on the carriageway he is leaving, and cycles and mopeds on cycle tracks crossing the carriageway he enters, to pass.

Rules.Title: No abrupt braking
Rules.Text: No driver of a vehicle shall brake abruptly unless it is necessary to do so for safety reasons.

Rules.Title: Slowing down with warning
Rules.Text: A driver intending to slow down appreciably shall first make sure he can do so without danger and give warning; the stop lights give that warning.

Rules.Title: Approach intersections able to stop
Rules.Text: Every driver approaching an intersection shall exercise extra care and drive at such a speed as to be able to stop to allow vehicles having the right of way to pass.

Rules.Title: From a path or earth-track, give way
Rules.Text: Every driver emerging from a path or an earth-track on to another road shall give way to vehicles travelling on that road.

Rules.Title: From a property, give way
Rules.Text: Every driver emerging on to a road from a property bordering thereon shall give way to vehicles travelling on that road.

Rules.Title: Unsigned intersections: priority rule
Rules.Text: Where traffic keeps to the right, the driver shall give way at intersections (other than from paths, tracks and motorway entries) to vehicles approaching from his right; where traffic keeps to the left, the right of way is regulated domestically.

Rules.Title: Do not enter a blocked intersection
Rules.Text: Even if traffic lights authorize him, a driver shall not enter an intersection if he will probably be obliged to stop on it, obstructing cross traffic.

Rules.Title: Clearing a signalled intersection
Rules.Text: A driver who has entered a signalled intersection may clear it without waiting for his direction to open, provided he does not impede road-users moving in the open direction.

Rules.Title: Give way to rail-borne vehicles
Rules.Text: At intersections, drivers of vehicles not moving on rails shall give way to rail-borne vehicles.

Rules.Title: Level-crossings
Rules.Text: Moderate speed; no entry while gates or half-gates are down, closing or rising; without gates or lights, enter only after making sure no train approaches; do not linger; if stopped, move off the track or warn the train.

Rules.Title: Pedestrians on pavements, else at the edge
Rules.Text: Pedestrians use pavements or verges where there are any; otherwise they may walk on the carriageway, as close as possible to its edge (recommended: facing the traffic).

Rules.Title: Pedestrians crossing
Rules.Text: Pedestrians shall not step on to the carriageway without care; they use a crossing nearby, obey its lights, take approaching vehicles into account, and do not linger.

Rules.Title: Signalled crossing: stop when forbidden, let pedestrians pass
Rules.Text: At a crossing regulated by lights or an official, drivers forbidden to proceed stop short of it; when allowed, they do not obstruct pedestrians on it; turning drivers give way to pedestrians using or about to use it.

Rules.Title: Unsignalled crossing: approach slowly, stop for pedestrians
Rules.Text: At an unregulated crossing, drivers approach only at a speed low enough not to endanger pedestrians using or about to use it and, if necessary, stop to let them cross.

Rules.Title: Passengers at a bus stop
Rules.Text: Drivers intending to overtake on the traffic side a public transport vehicle at a marked stop shall slow down and if necessary stop to allow passengers to board or alight.

Rules.Title: Stricter pedestrian priority allowed
Rules.Text: Contracting Parties may require drivers to stop in all cases when pedestrians are on or stepping on to a crossing, and to let pedestrians crossing at or very near an intersection pass.

Rules.Title: Islands on the carriageway
Rules.Text: A driver may pass either side of islands and posts, except where a sign shows the side, or the island is on the centreline of a two-way carriageway: then keep to its traffic side.

Rules.Title: Standing and parking: off the carriageway, else at the edge
Rules.Text: Outside built-up areas, stand or park off the carriageway as far as possible, never on cycle tracks; on the carriageway, as close as possible to the edge of the traffic side, parallel to it, not two abreast.

Rules.Title: Where standing or parking is prohibited
Rules.Text: No standing on pedestrian, cycle or level crossings, on or near rail tracks, under flyovers and in tunnels, near crests and blind bends, beside a no-crossing marking leaving less than 3 m; no parking near level-crossings, intersections and stops, before entries, where it blocks others, on priority roads outside built-up areas, or hiding signs.

Rules.Title: Leaving the vehicle
Rules.Text: A driver shall not leave his vehicle without suitable precautions against accidents and, for a motor vehicle, against its unauthorized use.

Rules.Title: Warning device when stationary
Rules.Text: A power-driven vehicle stationary on the carriageway outside a built-up area, at night unseen or where standing is prohibited, is signalled by a warning device at a sufficient distance.

Rules.Title: Opening of doors
Rules.Text: It shall be prohibited to open the door of a vehicle, to leave it open, or to alight without having made sure that to do so cannot endanger other road-users.

Rules.Title: Motorways: who may use them, no stopping, no U-turns
Rules.Text: On motorways: no pedestrians, animals, cycles, slow vehicles; no standing or parking outside marked sites (move off and warn if forced to stop); no U-turns, no reversing, no driving on the central strip.

Rules.Title: Entering a motorway
Rules.Text: Without an acceleration lane, give way to vehicles on the motorway; with one, use it and merge as Article 14, paragraphs 1 and 3, require.

Rules.Title: Leaving a motorway
Rules.Text: A driver leaving a motorway shall move into the lane of the exit in good time and enter the deceleration lane as soon as he can.

Rules.Title: Do not cut across processions
Rules.Text: It shall be prohibited to cut across troop columns, files of school-children accompanied by a person in charge, and other processions; persons in invalid chairs may use pavements.

Rules.Title: Cyclists, moped drivers, motor cyclists
Rules.Text: Hold the handlebars, no towing, no hampering loads, passengers only as allowed; cyclists may be required to use cycle tracks; Contracting Parties may allow cycling two abreast.

Rules.Title: Audible and luminous warnings
Rules.Text: Audible warnings only to avoid an accident or, outside built-up areas, to warn a driver he is about to be overtaken, not prolonged; luminous warnings instead between nightfall and dawn.

Rules.Title: Clear the track for trams
Rules.Text: Where a railway uses a carriageway, every road-user shall, on the approach of a tram or other rail-borne vehicle, clear the track as soon as possible.

Rules.Title: Loading of vehicles
Rules.Text: Never above the permissible maximum weight; the load stowed so as not to endanger, obstruct the view, cause nuisance or mask lights and plates; projections marked (more than 1 m front or rear; more than 0.40 m laterally at night).

Rules.Title: Behaviour in case of accident
Rules.Text: Stop without additional danger; make the site safe and keep its traces if someone was killed or seriously injured; identify oneself if asked; notify the police and stay if someone was injured or killed.

Rules.Title: Lighting at night
Rules.Text: Between nightfall and dawn, and when visibility is inadequate (fog, snowfall, heavy rain, tunnel), vehicles show white or selective-yellow lights to the front and red to the rear; never red to the front or white to the rear.

Rules.Title: Use of the lights
Rules.Text: No driving lights where the road is adequately lit or when standing; dip them when passing or following closely; passing lights otherwise; fog lights only in fog, snowfall or heavy rain.

Rules.Title: Make room for priority vehicles
Rules.Text: When warned of the approach of a priority vehicle by its special luminous and audible warning devices, every road-user shall leave room clear for it to pass and shall, if necessary, stop.

Rules.Title: Passing road works equipment
Rules.Text: To overtake or pass road works equipment at work, other drivers may, to the extent necessary and with all due precautions, disregard Articles 11 and 12.

Rules.Title: Automated driving
Rules.Text: The requirement that every moving vehicle shall have a driver is deemed to be satisfied while the vehicle is using an automated driving system which complies with domestic technical regulations and any applicable international legal instrument, and with domestic legislation governing operation; the effect is limited to the territory of that Contracting Party.
